segments.text: Okay we'll start with English questions and then switch to Polish at the end.
Maya through to your first Grand Slam semi-final here at Roland Garros.
Just focusing on today's match, what do you think you did well and what gave you an advantage?
Yeah definitely very challenging one. The conditions were very very tough,
it was very windy today so you just need to be very focused, like extra focused in
these kind of conditions so yeah I feel like what I did well was just stay calm
when when there was like 5-1 up and Anna I think she started to play much
more aggressive and it was 5-1 I think I'm just very proud that I stayed
composed you know and managed to win this set and you know then the second
set was was just a battle so I'm very happy, happy to win.
Emma Raducanu became or is the only woman to win a slam as a qualifier. You
could emulate that this weekend. What do you remember of her run to the US
Open five years ago and what inspiration do you think you're giving
to people that perhaps have to come through the qualifying phases? Yeah I
I mean, it was such an impressive run.
Also, she was so young.
I think she was 19, right?
Do I remember correctly?
So, yeah, I think she didn't drop a set as well.
So it was just incredible.
Yeah, I mean, what I, what was the question exactly?
Inspiration from her?
Oh, for me, from her.
In general. Well I feel like it's just, you know, I think the level is like very
close like the qualifying is not like much worse than the main draw and the
players in the qualifying they are so good as well. They are great
competitors and we just need to kind of believe and you know fight and just
believe that maybe someday it will click for us as well.
Yeah, that's what I would take from this experience.
You said on court after the match, you couldn't believe it.
Can you believe it now?
I mean, how do you feel about it now?
It's about an hour afterwards.
But can you take it in that you've got this far?
Not really.
I feel like I just, for some reason, I don't process it.
You know, like I'm just focusing on every single match.
And I honestly don't feel like it's
like a huge, huge moment for me.
But definitely after the tournament finishes,
I will kind of like have time to, I guess,
be grateful for what happened and process it as well.
But for now, I'm just very happy.
But I need I know that I need to focus on the job
Congratulations, I think one of the shots that worked really effectively today was kind of your backhand slice in terms of the spin that
You put on it when it would bounce on like the clay
I'm just curious. How do you think that shots evolved for you over your career?
And why do you think it worked effectively against Anna's game?
You mean slice and topspin like my backhand?
I mean, it's just my game. You know, I just try to
change the rhythm a lot.
I feel like it's pretty tough to play against this kind of style
because you don't have any rhythm and you just need to be very focused
because every ball can be different.
So yeah, I'm aware that it can be very annoying
for other players and I just try to use it
as much as I can.
I know people have been talking about the time you took away from the sport for your
mental health.
I wonder what mental work you're doing now, like you said, in this very overwhelming
situation and such a different part of your career.
You don't seem overwhelmed at all.
To be honest, I'm not really in the social media, I would say.
And yeah, I feel like it would be too much for me
at this moment.
So that's one of the things that I'm doing now
is just, I post and then I quit.
Yeah, other than that, I have a great people around me
that are with me for many, many, many years.
So I can trust them and tell them anything that I feel
be honest, so I feel like it's crucial in this situation and yeah that's that's pretty much it.
Hi Maya, sorry if you've been asked this this week but I wanted to ask you about your time
away from the sport and just how difficult was that and I guess it must be such a
contrast to everything you're kind of living now. Well the break wasn't very tough
like the tough moments were before the break, I would say.
I was struggling a lot.
You know, I pushed at the beginning.
I thought that I just need to stay very strong, tough,
and just keep practicing.
Yeah, but then I just couldn't get out of bed anymore.
I was just lifeless, to be honest.
And yeah, I just I knew that I need to take a break because otherwise I'm just not able to
like live I think so
Yeah, I needed to take a break
And I honestly didn't know if I'm gonna come back or not
To be like honest with you
Yeah, but after like months I decided to come back
I needed to kind of
figure a few things in my head, I would say. Yeah, and I came back. I'm happy that
I did.
Congratulations. I wanted to ask you what you're most proud of through this
run here, and also you said that you stepped away, that you're not
really on social media. Were you at some point in social media and then
went out of it or is it something that you just choose not to do? Well I choose
I mean I post post something and then I choose to quit because I just really
want to focus on my game like I want to leave French Open this year without
any regrets you know like I just want to give my all and I know that it
can be social media can be like a bit of overwhelming in this kind of
situation. So I try to give myself the best chance to play the best tennis that I can.
And what was the other question? Oh, okay. I guess that, you know, it's a long tournament.
I'm here almost three weeks now. And every day is different. Every match is different.
conditions are different so I had I had to adapt a lot and I'm very happy that I
was able to do that I think it's it's something that I can be proud of you
know and my effort to do that
precisely if we had met three weeks ago here before the qualities and if I
asked you about your form, your goals, your drive.
What would you have told me genuinely
on where you were in your career and your goals?
Well, my goal was to be top 100 this year.
That was the main goal.
Coming here, my goal was to qualify.
I felt like I'm doing a good job, that I
do the right things and I just need to be patient for it to click yeah but
honestly like obviously I didn't expect it to happen that way but I mean I'm
not complaining so yeah yeah
Hi Maya, here, sorry, congratulations. A Polish player performing well in Paris that
sounds familiar obviously and you receive any guidance from Iga because
you're about the same age and you've played together for many many years now?
Not really just, I mean, congratulations and this kind of stuff.
And another one, just from a physical point of view, how do you feel because you've been playing eight matches in your eight victories
and the rehab period is really short before tomorrow's semi-final, so what will you do to...
I mean, obviously I'm a bit tired, but that's normal.
but you know it's a grand slam so I feel like the adrenaline is very high and
like I can feel terrible but then I just step on the court and you know
it's a different story so it doesn't matter how I feel it's gonna be okay.
